title: Lament for Thaevalis
author: Ivaren of the Waking Houses
pages: Iriavel, where are your lamps? The amethyst is dark in the high halls. The trees we sang into arches have grown wild, and the deer sleep in the Council of Stars.
We gave our light to bind the Fallen. We gave our children's light as well. Each spring there are fewer cradles in the Starwood, and the Eldest call it the Debt of Light.
The Dimming Houses go into dream and do not wake. They say the world belongs to the young ones now. I say a debt is not paid by hiding from the creditor. I say we walk out and help.
Sing it slow, for there are few of us left to sing it. Thaevalis was a lamp among the trees. Let it be a lamp again, even a small one, even in a burrow, even in a human town.
